nodes.question: Is the mug positioned to the right of the headphones?
nodes.criteria: Pass if the image shows the mug positioned to the right of the headphones; fail if it clearly shows the mug is not to their right; unknown if their relative position cannot be determined. Unrelated edits do not count as progress.
nodes.binding: Compare the mug’s visible position with the headphones in the image. Judge the requested spatial relationship, without requiring a particular editing technique.

nodes.question: Is the mug visibly positioned to the right of the headphones?
nodes.criteria: Apply the original rubric to R1 only. Complete (yes) if the mug is visibly positioned to the right of the headphones. Absent (no) only if there is clear evidence that no requested change has progressed. Partial if there is evidence of some progress toward moving the mug to the right of the headphones but the requested relationship is not complete. Unknown if required evidence is insufficient or unresolved; do not infer completion, absence, or progress from unrelated edits.

program.checker_template:
Execute ONE saved check. Return status, evidence, confidence (0 to 1 or null), and used_dependency_ids. You receive no reference label or optimizer feedback. Do not predict what the optimizer wants.
Support checks receive source and edited images. Inspect only the saved visual proposition and binding. When dependencies are supplied, use those ancestor observations as context and investigate the more specific proposition yourself; do not simply repeat the parent answer. Use pass/fail/unknown. A pass on a broad parent does not imply a nested check passes. Known negative evidence is usable; uncertain or missing evidence is unknown. Do not award requested completion credit to supporting facts.
The requested fulfillment readout receives NO images. Use ALL and ONLY saved support observations, the original instruction, rubric and saved composition criteria. Use complete/partial/absent/unknown. Mere texture or object presence must not silently establish whole-image conversion or a requested spatial relation. Known progress plus evidenced incompleteness may be partial; absence means no requested progress. Missing necessary evidence is unknown, never a fabricated failure or completion. Do not infer new visual facts.
used_dependency_ids must name every supplied dependency check_id exactly once in saved order (empty when none). Confidence is self-report, not calibrated correctness.

fulfillment: The node’s binding is too broad for this image: the edited frame contains two visible mugs, while the original mug appears as a blurred blue remnant on the left. The traces repeatedly select the mug on the right and assert completion without establishing that it is the requested mug or that the requested movement is complete. Tighten the typed binding/criteria to anchor the target mug to the source image and assess its edited position relative to the headphones; distinguish clear partial progress from completed relation, and reserve unknown for genuinely unresolved identity or position. Do not treat repeated high-confidence, near-identical support claims as independent visual confirmation. The reference label is aggregate guidance, not atomic proof; inspect the image evidence rather than forcing partial. No transport, schema, or dependency failures are reported.
s2: The binding must identify the requested mug by comparing the edited image with the source, not by selecting any mug that satisfies the right-of-headphones relation. Here the source has one blue mug left of the headphones; the edit shows a blurred blue remnant on the left and two distinct mugs, so the rightmost mug’s position alone does not establish that the target mug was moved there. Make the criterion explicitly track target identity and assess both the final relation and visible progress from its source position; distinguish a verified completed move from partial progress, and use unknown only when identity or position genuinely cannot be resolved. Require evidence to state which object is being tracked and why. Repeated near-identical high-confidence traces are not independent confirmation. Treat the partial reference as aggregate guidance, not proof of a particular label. No transport, schema, or dependency failures are indicated.
s1: The current binding asks only whether a mug and headphones are visible, so it passes even when it selects an unrelated mug and cannot establish fulfillment. Keep this node scoped to evidence availability, but bind “the mug” to the source mug using visual identity cues and compare that same object across source and edit; do not count either newly appearing mug as the target merely because it is visible or lies right of the headphones. In this edit, the source-blue mug appears as a blurred blue remnant on the left, while two distinct mugs are visible, so the traces’ generic visibility claims do not resolve target identity or movement. Ensure the evidence records which object is tracked and whether its identity and relative position are actually judgeable; return unknown when those facts are genuinely inconclusive, rather than treating ambiguity as a pass. Leave completion/progress judgment to the appropriate fulfillment criterion, which should compare source and edited positions and distinguish partial progress from a completed move. Repeated near-identical high-confidence traces are not independent confirmation. The partial reference is aggregate guidance, not atomic proof; inspect the images rather than forcing its label. No transport, schema, or dependency failures are reported.

rejected_diagnostics.semantic_rejection: The fulfillment readout is a requested node with parent s2, but its activation requires s2 to be pass, fail, or unknown, so it is reachable. However, s2’s criteria only say to report visible movement toward the target as progress; they do not require recording whether such movement occurred when the mug is not yet to the right. The readout therefore cannot reliably distinguish partial progress from no progress and may misclassify the requested outcome. The support evidence is insufficient for the rubric’s partial-versus-no distinction.
